How To Conduct an Employee Performance Review

A useful performance review should give employees specific feedback they can understand and act on. In this video, learn a four-stage framework for conducting employee performance reviews: prepare with evidence from the full review period, open the meeting as a two-way conversation, structure feedback using the Situation-Behavior-Impact (SBI) model, and close by setting SMART goals and scheduling follow-up. The video also covers self-assessments, recency bias, documentation, development actions, and ongoing check-ins after the meeting. For ready-to-use language and a deeper framework, read the complete performance review guide. For ongoing review cycles, goal tracking, and one-on-one meetings, explore Paychex Flex Engage and broader Paychex Talent Management solutions.

Why Vague Performance Review Feedback Falls Flat

0:00 Here’s the truth: too many performance reviews end with feedback like, “You’re doing great, just be more of a team player.” Well-meant. Impossible to act on. The fix? A four-stage framework that turns feedback into results. Let’s walk through it.

Stage 1: Preparing for a Performance Review

0:17 Stage one starts before you sit down. Gather evidence from the whole review period: project results, peer input, past check-ins.

0:24 Send a self-assessment five to seven days ahead, so you both walk in ready. Then check yourself for bias. Is one rough week drowning out eleven strong months? That’s recency bias.

0:36 Picture a landscaping company owner getting ready to review her crew lead. Instead of working from memory, she pulls up a year of check-in notes. Now the review isn’t “I think.” It’s “here’s what happened.”

Stage 2: Opening the Review Conversation

0:48 Stage two: the first five minutes. Share the purpose and the time frame, preview what you’ll cover, and make it clear this is a conversation. Then hand it over: “Walk me through your self-assessment. How do you feel the year went?” Their view first. Yours second.

Stage 3: The SBI Feedback Model

1:04 Stage three is the main event. Use the SBI feedback model: Situation, Behavior, Impact. Balance recognition with development, so they know what to keep doing and what to change.

1:16 For our crew lead, “You’re doing great” becomes: “During the spring rush, you trained two new hires without being asked, and both crews stayed on schedule.” And “be more of a team player” becomes: “On last month’s jobs, client updates went out a day late, so the install crew showed up without the plans.” Specific. Fair. Fixable.

Stage 4: Setting SMART Goals Together

1:36 Stage four: close with goals. Agree on two to four SMART goals together and leave room for their questions and ideas. Before anyone leaves, put the first check-in on the calendar. Then end on a constructive note: recognize their strengths and offer support where they want to grow.

What To Do After the Performance Review

1:52 The meeting ends, but the follow-through doesn’t. Document the conversation and share written notes for the employee to review. Turn each growth area into a concrete action, like training, a stretch assignment, or coaching. Keep check-ins going monthly or quarterly. And if pay or performance concerns come up, bring in HR.

How Paychex Can Help

2:11 That’s a lot to juggle. Paychex performance management tools keep reviews, goal tracking, and one-on-ones in one place, right inside Paychex Flex, our all-in-one payroll and HR platform. It’s powered by Paychex WISE, our AI engine. So, when an employee asks, “What’s next for me?” AI can draft a career track with the skills for each level. AI drafts. You decide. And for expert guidance, Paychex HR professionals can help you shape the process.

Recap

2:39 Before you go, let’s put it all together: prep with evidence, open with a conversation, give feedback with SBI, and close with goals and a date on the calendar. Do that, and your next review won’t just grade the past year. It’ll shape the year ahead.

Wrap Up

2:55 Need help finding the right words? The full guide has sample phrases you can use during your next review. It’s linked below. And don’t forget to subscribe for more ways to lead your team with confidence.
